Name: Falcon Mega Solutions - Vessel Tracking & Satellite Communication
Description:
Falcon Mega Solutions (FMS) delivers satellite-based vessel tracking and maritime security systems to ship owners, fleet managers, and fishing operators in 40+ countries.

Founded in 2012, we have secured 2,900+ vessels and operate a global network of service partners worldwide.

OUR PLATFORM: Falcon Mega Track (FMT)
A web and mobile tracking platform providing real-time global vessel positions, live weather overlay, OceanWise nautical charts, 2-year track history, and voyage reports — all in one screen.

OUR SERVICES:
  Satellite AIS Tracking — global coverage, no new hardware, uses existing Class-A AIS
  Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) — IMO/SOLAS compliant hardware and monitoring
  Sat-C SSAS Integration — vessel tracking via existing Inmarsat-C terminals
  Fishing Zone Alert System (FZAS) — zone alerts and compliance for fishing fleets
  V-Mail — compressed satellite email for vessels (80%+ data savings)

TECHNOLOGY PARTNERS:
Iridium | Inmarsat | OceanWise (Nautical Charts) | PRS 

SERVICE PARTNERS WANTED:
We work through marine electronics companies, communication, and navigation equipment suppliers globally.

Apply at: falconmegasolutions.com

Contact: sales@falconmegasolutions.com  |  www.falconmegasolutions.com

Name: Lacuna Space
Description:
Redefining the possibilities of global connectivity, Lacuna Space offers low-cost, simple, and reliable solutions for sensors and mobile equipment. The Lacuna Network is designed to work everywhere, and all the time, so you can focus on using data from your sensors or tracking the status of your moving assets.

- Smart automatic connection - no user required. No manual fumbling between 4G or Wi-Fi!

Name: Satcenter

Name: Von Storch Engineering
Description:
Von Storch Engineering provides specialized services for the aerospace industry. With extensive experience tracking spacecraft, launch vehicles, and aircraft, we’re well-equipped to handle diverse challenges and mission needs. Our Ground Station Services support a wide range of applications, from satellite communication to aircraft downlinks.

Our main services include:
● Dedicated & On-Demand ground station receiving services for spacecraft & launch vehicles (S-Band, UHF/VHF, L-/C-/X-Band).
● Lost satellite support: If a customer hasn't established contact or lost contact with their satellite, we offer extensive searches for any weak RF signals, help locate the satellite in orbit and re-establish communications.
● Dedicated tracking support for satellite operators in the weeks after launch. We perform frequent tracking measurements and keep track of our customers satellites in orbit. Significantly reducing operations risks and ensuring stable RF communications.
● Object Identification: We accurately and quickly identify which object the customers satellite is after launch. - Allowing for smooth and fast-paced OPS and improving space-safety for our customer and everyone else in orbit.
● Space Domain Awareness (SDA/SSA): RF sensor-as-a-service, Tracking, Object ID and spectrum monitoring offerings for space situational awareness.
● On-demand ground station receiving services of long-range line-of-sight RF downlinks from aerial vehicles. Over distances of hundreds of kilometers we can receive secure live video/data feeds from fixed wing aircraft/helicopters/UAVs and forward this to an operations center. This is often used in Search & Rescue, Disaster response or broadcast events.

Whether you’re planning your next mission or need urgent support, we’re flexible. Get in touch — we’d love to support your operations.

Name: Hydramo
Description:
Hydramo is a deep-tech Earth Observation startup focused on delivering operational intelligence for both mission-critical response and everyday environmental management directly to citizens. We believe that environmental awareness and real action starts with people themselves.


We develop next-generation solutions that combine satellite observations, in-situ sensing and edge processing to enable real-time environmental awareness — even where connectivity is limited or unavailable.

Our EO2GO platform delivers actionable Earth Observation insights directly to citizens, emergency responders, vehicles and field teams. EO2GO supports two flagship domains: civil protection and environmental monitoring, enabling applications in disaster early warning, flood response, agriculture monitoring, water management, fisheries and ecosystem health.

Hydramo contributes to the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative by supporting Pillars 2, 3 and 4, bridging space-based data, local sensing and field-level action. Our technologies support climate adaptation, food and water security, environmental monitoring and operational decision-making.

We are committed to bringing satellite intelligence closer to people — supporting safer, more resilient and sustainable communities worldwide.

Name: Optical Wireless Superhighways FREE
Description: Data generation and consumption have been growing exponentially over the past 50 years. Traditional technologies to disseminate data at all length scales have or will shortly reach their capacity limits. To support future applications, such as high-resolution earth observation, 5G and beyond wireless connectivity, and data-intensive remote services in homes, a new paradigm for wireless connectivity is needed. Building on the unique Dutch eco-system of optical systems academic research intertwined with industrial optical wireless R&D, we can put the Netherlands within 5 years at the forefront of wireless communication technology. A key objective of this transition is to provide a single, multi-technology network, including satellites as critical components. we will carry out exploratory and applied research into crucial aspects of deploying optical communications to replace radio frequency for wireless connectivity. We will use 5G as a network of networks to seamlessly integrate satellite communications into ground networks to provide satellite-to-satellite Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) and Software-Defined Networking (SDN). This simpler integration between terrestrial and satellite networks allows new growth potential for the Internet of Things (IOT). Using the huge available bandwidth, inherent security, low latency, and license-free exploitation, we foresee a 10 to 100-fold increase in wireless connectivity at all length scales, from several meters to tens of thousands of kilometers. Many synergies can be achieved by a joint pursuit of innovation in the terminals used, a better understanding of the links and a holistic approach to resilient networking, architecture, and system integration.
